paragraphs: The Coombe is a hospital in Dublin where babies are born. This year it is 200 years old.
In the winter of 1825, there was a big snowstorm. Two pregnant women tried to walk to a hospital across the city. They died in the cold, and their babies died too.
A local woman, Margaret Boyle, wanted to help. She asked a doctor for space in his building. The new hospital started with one room and 15 beds.

Today, giving birth is much safer. In the 1930s, about one mother in 181 died. Now it is about one in 31,000. In 2024, a very small baby called Ollie was born there at 22 weeks. He weighed only 420 grams, but he lived.
A museum in Dublin has a show about the hospital's history.
sentZh: 庫姆是都柏林一家迎接嬰兒出生的醫院。
今年它已經200歲了。
1825年冬天，發生了一場大暴風雪。
兩名孕婦試圖步行到城市另一頭的醫院。
她們在寒冷中死去，她們的嬰兒也死了。
當地一位名叫瑪格麗特．博伊爾的女性想要幫忙。
她向一位醫生要求在他的建築裡提供空間。
新醫院一開始只有一個房間和15張床。
如今，生產安全多了。
在1930年代，大約每181位母親就有一位死亡。
現在大約是三萬一千分之一。
2024年，一個名叫奧利的極小嬰兒在那裡於22週時出生。
他只有420公克重，但他活了下來。
都柏林一家博物館正在舉辦關於這家醫院歷史的展覽。

paragraphs: The Coombe, one of Dublin's main maternity hospitals, is celebrating 200 years. Its story began with a sad event in the winter of 1825, when a heavy snowstorm hit the city. Two pregnant women from the Liberties area tried to walk to the Rotunda, the only maternity hospital in Dublin at the time. They died in the cold on Thomas Street, and their babies died too.

A local woman, Margaret Boyle, was so upset that she asked Dr John Kirby to give some space in his medical school to poor mothers. He agreed, and the hospital started with one ward of 15 beds. In 1829 four new wards opened, and it became the first maternity hospital south of the River Liffey. In 1967 it moved to a large new building on Cork Street.

Having a baby is now far safer. Between 1928 and 1935, one mother in 181 died, but between 2020 and 2023 the figure was one in 31,063. In 2024, a baby called Ollie was born at 22 weeks, weighing just 420 grams. He is the most premature baby to survive at the hospital, and he turned two in August.
The Little Museum of Dublin has opened an exhibition about the hospital and about Margaret Boyle, whose story is not well known.

他答應了，醫院一開始只有一間15張床的病房。
1829年開設了四間新病房，它成為利菲河以南第一家婦產醫院。
1967年，它搬到庫克街一棟大型新建築。
現在生孩子安全得多。

paragraphs: The Coombe, one of Dublin's leading maternity hospitals, is marking its bicentenary. Its origins lie in a tragedy during the winter of 1825, when two pregnant women from the Liberties set out through a snowstorm for the Rotunda, then the city's only dedicated maternity hospital. They collapsed on Thomas Street and died from exposure, along with their unborn babies.

Deeply affected, local resident Margaret Boyle persuaded Dr John Kirby to make room in his anatomy school for poor women in labour. The service opened with a single 15-bed ward, and in 1829 four new wards made it the first maternity hospital south of the Liffey. It later relocated to a purpose-built site on Cork Street in 1967.

Medical progress since then has been dramatic. Between 1928 and 1935, one mother in 181 died, compared with one in 31,063 between 2020 and 2023. In 2024 a boy named Ollie was born at 22 weeks, weighing only 420 grams; he is the most premature baby to survive at the hospital and celebrated his second birthday in August.
A new exhibition at the Little Museum of Dublin traces the hospital's history and highlights Margaret Boyle, a founder largely overlooked by official records.

They succumbed to exposure on Thomas Street, and their unborn infants perished with them.

It eventually decamped to a purpose-built site on Cork Street in 1967.
